Custom Roll Stock Film: Printing Options, Color Count and Minimums

Published August 24, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

For printed roll stock, compare rotogravure and flexo by color count, volume and detail: gravure suits long runs with fine detail; flexo suits shorter runs and faster changes. Confirm cylinder or plate costs, repeat length, and whether your design fits the press width before quoting.

Decision table

FactorRotogravureFlexo
Run lengthLong runs economicalShort to medium
Color detailVery fine, consistentGood, process-dependent
Setup costHigher cylinder costLower plate cost
ChangeoverSlowerFaster
Best forLarge volume, premium printFlexible orders

Match print method to volume

Rotogravure delivers excellent color depth at high volumes but carries cylinder costs. Flexo suits shorter runs and quicker artwork changes. Ask suppliers for a cost comparison at your expected volume before choosing.

Design for the press

Confirm the press width, repeat length and number of colors available. Design artwork within those limits to avoid expensive over-width printing or extra color passes.

Color and lamination interaction

Print color appears different after lamination and coating. Approve a printed and laminated proof, and confirm barrier layers do not affect print adhesion.

Minimums and reorders

Confirm minimum meters per order and whether cylinders or plates are stored for reorders. Keep artwork and color standards with the supplier for consistent repeats.

Buyer checklist

  1. Compare gravure vs flexo at your volume
  2. Confirm press width and repeat
  3. Approve a laminated proof
  4. Check color count fits
  5. Confirm reorder terms

Frequently asked questions

Gravure or flexo: which is better?

Gravure gives finer detail at high volume; flexo is more flexible for shorter runs. Compare cost at your volume.

What is a repeat length?

The printed pattern length on the roll; your artwork and pouch size must fit the press repeat.

Can I reorder the same film later?

Yes, if cylinders or plates are stored; confirm storage terms and keep color standards.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Roll stock film printing is a materials and ink-count decision. Films available include PET / AL / PE barrier films, kraft with PLA liner and metallized films, printed offset, flexo or digital at 1–8 colors with CMYK + Pantone matching. Finishes range from matte and gloss lamination to soft-touch, spot UV, foil stamping and embossing. MOQ is 500 PCS per custom size and artwork; sampling takes 5–7 working days after artwork confirmation and production 2–4 weeks. Compliance statements — FDA-compliant inks and materials, MSDS and test reports — are provided on request.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many colors can roll stock be printed in?

Offset, flexo or digital printing supports 1–8 colors with CMYK + Pantone matching.

What finishes are available on roll film?

Matte or gloss lamination, soft-touch, spot UV, foil stamping and embossing or debossing.
